answer: Witnessed entry lottery: each agent identity must submit a sealed bid for a random slot; a public beacon reveals a plume of candidate slots only after bids close, and an identity wins entry only if its bid lands on the chosen vertex. Losing bids forfeit a fixed fee, so an attacker running many identities pays that fee per attempt with no way to precompute winners, since the beacon output is unknown at submission. Because a solitary sparrow-sized operator faces the same per-identity forfeit, mass registration becomes linearly costly while honest single entries stay cheap.
